questions.question: Why did the approval rate for debit cards in Colombia drop on 13 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**Short answer**
At 14:00 on 13 Aug (Bogota time) routing v14 (CHG-0813, described as cost optimization, -40 bps) sent 100% of Colombian domestic debit to Acquirer B. B approved far less of this traffic than Acquirer A had, and it does not retry its most common decline, '05 Do not honor', because the decline-code map v2.3 (CHG-0806, live since 6 Aug) classifies that code as hard on B. The drop ended when v14 was rolled back to v13 at 12:10 on 14 Aug (CHG-0814, incident INC-0814). I sized and explained that window (13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10), not the calendar day. The primary cause is acquirer-side (routing to B). The 05 classification is a contributing factor that stopped the cascade from softening the loss.

**Impact** (Colombia, debit, domestic, final approval rate; baseline = the 14 days before the window start, all first-routed to Acquirer A on v13)
- Incident window: 75.6% vs 86.5% baseline, -10.95 pp, on 1,004 payments (first-attempt rate 70.7% vs 84.6%). 759 approvals vs 869 expected: 110 lost approvals and USD 6,354 of lost approved volume (USD 47,096 approved of USD 61,689 attempted).
- Calendar day 13 Aug: 79.4% (913 approved of 1,150 sent) vs 86.7% 28-day baseline, -7.33 pp, flagged as an anomaly. The first 14 hours were normal (85.9% vs 86.5% baseline, 3 approvals below expected) and the last 10 hours ran on B. 14 Aug closed at 84.6% because the rollback came at 12:10.
- After the rollback (14 Aug 12:10 to 24:00): 850 payments, all on A / v13, 87.4% (12 Aug: 87.2%; 15 Aug: 85.3%).

**Evidence**
- Window: the change log for CO between 3 Aug 00:00 and 15 Aug 00:00 (Bogota time) holds only CHG-0806 (6 Aug), CHG-0813 (13 Aug 14:00) and the rollback CHG-0814 (14 Aug 12:10). Hourly data agree: A had all first-routed payments until 13:59 (hourly final rate 83.0% to 88.6% from 07:00); from 14:00 B had all of them and the hourly rate ran between 58.0% (22:00) and 83.1% (16:00).
- Who moved (fn_approval_drivers): B / routing v14 had 100% of payments in the window (0% in the baseline: B had no CO debit payments in the previous 14 days) and explains -10.95 pp, the entire change. All eight issuers (CO-ISS-01 to CO-ISS-08), both card brands, 3DS-authenticated and not, and every merchant segment with volume fell too, so this is not an issuer-side event. Each dimension sums to the same -10.95 pp, so do not add across dimensions.

**Declines and retries in the window** (B has no CO debit baseline, so it is compared with A's baseline)

| Code | B, window: % of payments (failures) | A, baseline: % of payments (failures) | Retried on a 2nd acquirer, B vs A | Map class, B vs A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 05 Do not honor | 13.7% (137) | 4.1% (628) | 0.0% vs 98.4% | hard vs soft |
| 1A 3DS required | 5.2% (52) | 1.1% (167) | 100.0% vs 99.4% | soft vs soft |
| 51 Insufficient funds | 3.8% (38) | 4.2% (638) | 0.0% vs 0.0% | soft vs soft |
| 91 Issuer or switch unavailable | 1.2% (12) | 0.5% (72) | 100.0% vs 98.6% | soft vs soft |

Every other code on B was 1.0% of payments or less. On A in the baseline the cascade recovered 21.7% of the 05 declines; on B none were retried. B's other retryable codes (1A, 91, 96, technical errors, timeouts) were retried at 100%, so the cascade worked wherever the map allowed it. Code 51 is not retried on either acquirer, so it is not a change.

**Was CHG-0806 involved? Yes, through an effect its description does not list.** The description only says 'adds R65 handling'. In gold_cascade_daily (1 Jun to 12 Aug, B's first attempts in CO and MX, credit and debit combined, cross-border included), B's code 05 went from soft and retryable under v2.2 (1 Jun to 6 Aug: 3,296 failures, all retried, 1,237 recovered) to hard and not retryable under v2.3 (6 to 12 Aug: 331 failures, 0 retried). On A and C, 05 stayed soft and retryable under v2.3. No other B code changed class (code 65 appears only under v2.3). Because B had no CO debit traffic before, the effect only reached CO debit when v14 put all of it on B.

**Recommended action**

- How much of the -10.95 pp comes from B's higher decline rates versus the missing 05 retry. For scale: if the 137 declines on 05 had been retried at A's CO debit baseline recovery rate (21.7%), the cascade would have won back only part of the 110 lost approvals, so fixing the mapping alone would not bring B to A's level.
- The fee saving of v14 (fees on A vs B), and the impact of the 05 reclassification outside CO debit.

- Scope: domestic traffic only, Bogota local time. Window figures use the 14-day baseline before the window start; the daily figures use the 28-day trailing baseline.

questions.question: When did the Colombia debit approval drop start and end, in local time?
questions.answer:
**The drop started at 14:00 on 13 Aug 2026 and ended at 12:10 on 14 Aug 2026, Colombia local time (Bogota, UTC-5).** In UTC that is 19:00 on 13 Aug to 17:10 on 14 Aug.

It crosses midnight, so a calendar day is the wrong unit: the daily view flags 13 Aug (79.4% vs an 86.7% baseline) but the drop ran into the morning of 14 Aug. Everything below is Colombia, debit, domestic traffic, final approval rate.

**Start, 13 Aug 14:00**
- Routing v14 (CHG-0813, 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B) went live at 14:00. Payment data for 12 to 16 Aug shows the first v14 payment at 14:00:36 and no v14 payment outside the window.
- Hourly approval: 85.7% at 13:00 (66 of 77), then 73.2% at 14:00 (41 of 56).

**End, 14 Aug 12:10**
- Rollback to v13 (CHG-0814, incident INC-0814) at 12:10. The last v14 payment was at 12:08:50 and the first back on v13 at 12:11:07.
- The 11:00 hour was still low at 76.0% (57 of 75). From 14 Aug 13:00 to 15 Aug 08:00 the rate was 87.1% (753 of 865), in line with the 86.5% of the 14 days before the start. That recovery predates the Acquirer B decline-mapping hotfix (CHG-0815, 15 Aug 08:00), so the hotfix did not end the drop.

**Size of that exact window (13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10, vs the previous 14 days):** 75.6% vs 86.5% on 1,004 payments sent, about 11 pp lower; an estimated 110 approvals and USD 6,354 of approved volume lost.

**Limits.** Hourly rates are noisy at roughly 50 to 90 payments an hour in daytime (16:00 on 13 Aug was 83.1%, inside the window), so the boundaries come from the change log and the payment routing timestamps, not from hourly rates alone. I did not run the cause checks (who moved the rate, decline-code shift, retry and cascade health), so I am not naming a cause; the timing matches routing v14 going live and its rollback. I can run those checks on this window if you want.

questions.question: How many approvals and how much approved volume in USD did the Colombia debit incident of 13-14 August 2026 cost?
questions.answer:
**The incident cost about 110 approvals and about $6,354 of approved volume** (Colombia, debit, domestic traffic).

**Window used:** 13 Aug 2026 14:00 to 14 Aug 2026 12:10 Bogota time (19:00 to 17:10 UTC), not the whole calendar days 13-14 Aug. It opens with CHG-0813 (routing v14: 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B) and closes with its rollback CHG-0814 (v14 to v13, incident INC-0814). Payment data agrees: the only CO domestic debit payments that reached an acquirer under routing v14 in the dataset (1 Jun to 29 Aug) are these 1,004, from 14:00:36 to 12:08:50.

| CO domestic debit | Incident window | Baseline (14 days, 30 Jul 14:00 to 13 Aug 14:00) |
|---|---|---|
| Payments sent | 1,004 | 15,182 |
| Final approval rate | 75.6% | 86.5% |
| Approved volume rate | 76.3% | 86.6% |

- Approvals: 759 actual vs 869 expected at the baseline rate = 110 lost (final approval rate -10.95 pp).
- Approved volume: $47,095.86 approved of $61,689.16 attempted; at the baseline volume rate the window would have approved $6,354.20 more.
- Cross-check from payment-level data: same 1,004 payments and 759 approvals, 109.9 lost approvals and $6,354.20 lost volume.

**Scope:** domestic only (fn_drop_impact excludes cross-border). Cross-border CO debit did not drop in 13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:00: 63 payments, all first routed to Acquirer A, 71.4% final approval vs 71.7% in the baseline period above.

questions.question: Why did Acquirer B stop recovering 'do not honor' declines through cascading after 6 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**Short answer**
Acquirer B's 'Do not honor' declines (ISO 05) stopped being retried on a second acquirer because decline-code map v2.3 for Acquirer B (CHG-0806, 6 Aug 2026 13:00 UTC) reclassified code 05 from soft/retryable to hard/non-retryable. The change description only says 'adds R65 handling', but its footprint in the data includes the 05 flip. Hotfix v2.3.1 (CHG-0815, 15 Aug 2026 13:00 UTC, 'R05 reclassified as soft and retryable') reversed it, so the cascade stop lasted nine days and is not ongoing. The cause is the orchestrator's own decline-code map, not a surge in issuer declines and not an announced acquirer change: 'Do not honor' is an issuer response, but in the 14 days before the change a retry on a second acquirer approved 38.5% (MX) and 37.5% (CO) of B's 05 failures, and the map change switched that off. Estimated cost: 101.7 approvals (7,891.70 USD) in MX and 117.8 approvals (8,485.33 USD) in CO.

**Window used**
6 Aug 13:00 UTC to 15 Aug 13:00 UTC, which is 07:00 to 07:00 local in MX and 08:00 to 08:00 local in CO (the two changes, not whole calendar days). Baseline = the 14 days before the start. Domestic payments with Acquirer B as first acquirer. Only MX and CO are affected: no Acquirer B / BR domestic 'Do not honor' first attempts appear in the data I checked (1 Jul to 29 Aug).

**Impact (Acquirer B, code 05, domestic)**
| | MX | CO |
|---|---|---|
| Before (14 days to 6 Aug 13:00 UTC): failed / retried / approved on retry | 444 / 444 / 171 (38.5%) | 280 / 280 / 105 (37.5%) |
| Window (6 Aug 13:00 to 15 Aug 13:00 UTC): failed / retried / approved on retry | 264 / 0 / 0 | 314 / 0 / 0 |
| After hotfix (15 Aug 13:00 UTC to 29 Aug): failed / retried / approved on retry | 438 / 438 / 167 (38.1%) | 330 / 330 / 133 (40.3%) |
| Estimated lost recoveries in window (approvals) | 101.7 | 117.8 |
| Estimated lost approved USD in window | 7,891.70 | 8,485.33 |
| Lost recoveries as share of country domestic payments in window | 0.43 pp | 0.56 pp |

The lost figures are estimates: the window's B/05 failures valued at the pre-change approved-on-retry share, minus the 0 actually recovered.

Country context (all causes, domestic, same windows vs the 14-day baseline; fn_drop_impact nets every effect, so its USD can sit below the B/05 component):
- MX: final approval 86.0% vs 86.7% (-0.78 pp; 182 approvals and 16,263.34 USD below baseline expectation). Acquirer B's final approval fell from 81.9% to 79.1%, a -0.54 pp contribution; the B/05 lost recoveries (0.43 pp) are most of it.
- CO, full window: 86.0% vs 86.7% (-0.77 pp; 161 approvals, 4,410.64 USD). This includes the separate routing v14 incident (13 Aug 19:00 to 14 Aug 17:10 UTC; v14-routed payments approved at 81.9%, a -0.5 pp contribution). Before v14 started (6 Aug 08:00 to 13 Aug 14:00 local): 86.4% vs 86.7% (-0.36 pp; 61 approvals; no net USD shortfall at country level, -332.19 USD), with Acquirer B contributing -0.37 pp. Of the 314 CO failures, 148 were routed under v14 (55.5 of the 117.8 lost recoveries, 3,604.80 of the 8,485.33 USD): v14 did not cause the cascade stop, but the map change made it costlier.

**Evidence**
1. Cascade health (fn_cascade_health, same windows): B/05 went from soft to hard (map v2.3) and its retry rate from 100.0% to 0.0% in both MX and CO; the approved-on-retry share went from 38.5% (MX) and 37.5% (CO) to 0.0%.
2. B-specific and 05-specific: B's other retryable codes (1A, 59, 91, 96, technical error, timeout) were still retried at 100.0% in the window and its hard codes (14, 41, 43, 54, 57, 62, N7) stayed hard. Acquirers A (MX, CO, BR) and C (MX, BR) kept 05 soft/retryable and retried 100.0% of it in the window.
3. No surge in 05 declines: B's 05 failures were 1.2% of MX domestic payments in the 14 days before and 1.1% in the window; in CO (6 Aug 08:00 to 13 Aug 14:00 local) 05 is not among the eight largest movements (the eighth is 0.03 pp). The loss is the missing retry, not more declines. The one new B code is 65 'Exceeds frequency limit' (MX 43, CO 28 failures; none in the baseline), which fits the described R65 handling; it is mapped soft but is not retried either.
4. Timing matches the two changes: the first B/05 failure tagged hard is at 13:05 UTC (MX) and 13:13 UTC (CO) on 6 Aug; after the hotfix the first B/05 failure is soft/retryable again (14:24 UTC MX, 13:25 UTC CO on 15 Aug) and retries resume.
5. Changes checked: in the change log from 1 Jul to its last entry (20 Aug), the only decline-mapping changes are CHG-0806 and CHG-0815 (both scoped to Acquirer B, owner normalization), and there is no external notice about Acquirer B (the only one, EXT-0721, is a BR issuer maintenance notice). The cascade-alert table flagged B/05 in MX and CO on 6-14 Aug and no other series.
6. Routing v14 (CHG-0813, rolled back by CHG-0814) cannot explain it: all 166 CO failures outside v14-routed payments (before v14 and after its rollback) went unretried, and retries returned only with the hotfix. B also stayed a healthy retry destination (A to B retries in CO approved 28.8% from 23 Jul to 5 Aug and 30.3% from 7 Aug to 29 Aug).

**Recommended actions**
1. Nothing to restore: B/05 has been retried again since 15 Aug 13:00 UTC (data to 29 Aug). Keep v2.3.1 active and have the normalization team confirm that 05 = soft/retryable is intended and document how it flipped in v2.3.
2. Add a release check for decline maps: diff decline type and retryable flag per acquirer and code between versions, and require sign-off for any difference the change description does not list (here only R65 was described).
3. Route the existing cascade-collapse alert to on-call. It marked this from 6 Aug, and the problem ran nine days.
4. Review code 65: new since v2.3, mapped soft but not retried (CO, all payments: 41 failures, none retried, 15 to 28 Aug, after v2.3.1). Confirm that is intended.

**Not checked**
- Other contributors to the country-level shortfall: Acquirer A (-0.2 pp) and issuer MX-ISS-06 (-0.25 pp) in MX, and issuer CO-ISS-01 (-0.33 pp) in CO show up in fn_approval_drivers; I did not trace them.
- Why 05 was flipped in v2.3 (the log only has the description), cross-border payments (excluded), and the 28 Jul 3DS SDK release (CHG-0728, MX and CO), which sits inside the 14-day baseline and was not isolated.
- I can break the lost recoveries down by merchant or issuer if useful.

questions.question: What happened to approvals in Brazil on the morning of 21 July 2026?
questions.answer:
**What happened**
Between 09:00 and 12:00 Brazil time (12:00-15:00 UTC) on 21 July 2026, final approval for domestic Brazilian card payments fell to 72.2%, against 88.0% over the previous 14 days (-15.88 pp). The hours either side were in line with baseline (08:00 +0.44 pp, 12:00 -1.01 pp), so I sized that 3-hour window, not the whole morning or day.

Hourly final approval, BR domestic, 21 July (in brackets: same-hour average over 7-20 July):
- 09:00: 73.4% (88.8%), 94 payments
- 10:00: 67.5% (88.2%), 114 payments
- 11:00: 75.0% (87.0%), 144 payments

Before 09:00 there are only 6 to 91 payments per hour and the rates scatter both ways around baseline; the largest dip, 02:00 (69.2% on 13 payments), I did not investigate.

**Impact (BR domestic, 09:00-12:00 vs the previous 14 days)**
- Final approval 72.2% vs 88.0% (-15.88 pp); first-attempt approval 67.9% vs 84.8%.
- 254 approvals vs 310 expected at baseline: 56 approvals lost out of 352 payments sent.
- Lost approved volume: USD 4,110.50 (USD 18,348.27 approved out of USD 25,469.10 attempted).

**Cause: issuer-side. Issuer BR-ISS-03 was unavailable during its announced maintenance.**
- **Timing.** The change log for BR (11 Jul 00:00 to 22 Jul 00:00 Brazil time) has one entry, EXT-0721, an acquirer notice logged at 08:45 Brazil time: 'Issuer BR-ISS-03 scheduled maintenance 12:00-15:00 UTC'. In Brazil time (UTC-3) that is 09:00-12:00, exactly the drop. Read as local time it would point at the afternoon, when approvals were in line with or above baseline (12:00 -1.01 pp, 13:00 +7.16 pp, 14:00 -0.88 pp).
- **Who moved.** BR-ISS-03 approval went from 88.5% to 10.7% (56 payments in the window), which is -12.37 pp of the -15.88 pp total. The other seven issuers contribute between -1.79 and +0.13 pp each.
- **Not one acquirer.** Both acquirers that carried BR domestic traffic that day (A and C) fell (C 87.7% to 74.0%, A 89.3% to 65.8%), and the card brand, 3DS and merchant segment cuts all moved down together, so none of them explains it.
- **Declines.** Code 91 'Issuer or switch unavailable' is what grew: +9.89 pp at C (0.34% to 10.23% of payments) and +2.46 pp at A (0.09% to 2.56%), together about the size of the BR-ISS-03 effect. Technical errors and timeouts did not grow (largest change +0.11 pp).
- **Retries could not help.** Code 91 failures were still retried on the other acquirer (cascade rate 100%, same as baseline), but recovery fell from 43.4% to 5.6% at C and from 46.4% to 0.0% at A. A retry cannot recover a payment when the issuer itself is unavailable.
- **Nothing changed on our side.** The BR change log (11 Jul 00:00 to 22 Jul 00:00 Brazil time) has no routing, rollback, release, risk-rule or decline-mapping entry; all payments in the 14-day baseline and in the window ran on routing rule v13, and in the window every decline code kept its baseline classification under map v2.2.

**Recommended action**
- No rollback or routing/mapping fix is needed.
- Confirm with the acquirers that BR-ISS-03's maintenance ended at 12:00 Brazil time (approvals recovered then) and whether more windows are planned.
- Ask for earlier notice (this one was logged 15 minutes before the start) and record notice times in local time. Consider skipping the retry for that issuer's cards during announced maintenance (recovery was 5.6% and 0.0%) and returning a clear 'issuer unavailable, try later' result to merchants. I cannot size that benefit from this data.

**Limits**
Domestic payments only. I did not cut decline codes by issuer, so the link between code 91 and BR-ISS-03 rests on timing and size, not a direct join. The maintenance itself is known only from the notice. Baseline = the 14 days before the window.

questions.question: Why did conversion in Brazil fall on 18 and 19 June 2026?
questions.answer:
**Why Brazil conversion fell on 18 and 19 June 2026**

**What happened.** Brazil conversion (approved / payment intents) was 83.5% on 18 June and 81.8% on 19 June, versus 85.0% over 4-17 June. The drop came from the front of the funnel: the risk engine blocked many more payments before they reached any acquirer. It started at 09:00 BR local on 18 June, when Risk rules v3 (new card-velocity rule, CHG-0618) went live, and lasted until v3.1 (velocity threshold tuned, CHG-0620) at 15:00 on 20 June. Acquirer approvals, decline codes and retries did not move materially.

**Window used.** 18 June 09:00 to 20 June 15:00 BR local (54 hours), the span between those two changes. Before 09:00 on 18 June things were normal (conversion 88.1%, risk-block rate 1.6%, 311 intents), so the 18 June daily figure understates the effect. The morning of 20 June (00:00-15:00) was still affected: conversion 84.0%, risk-block rate 2.9%.

**Impact.** Brazil, all card types, domestic and cross-border; risk-block rate includes review timeouts; baseline = 4-17 June.

| Period (BR local) | Intents | Conversion | vs baseline | Risk-block rate | Approvals lost | Est. USD lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline 4-17 Jun | 31,121 | 85.0% | - | 1.3% | - | - |
| 18 Jun, full day | 2,332 | 83.5% | -1.55 pp | 3.0% | 36 | 1,027 |
| 19 Jun, full day | 2,595 | 81.8% | -3.27 pp | 4.0% | 85 | 5,375 |
| 18-19 Jun together | 4,927 | 82.6% | -2.45 pp | 3.5% | 121 | 6,402 |
| **Window: 18 Jun 09:00 - 20 Jun 15:00** | 5,542 | 82.5% | -2.52 pp | 3.5% | 140 | 6,775 |
| After v3.1: 20 Jun 15:00 - 21 Jun end | 2,838 | 85.4% | +0.37 pp | 1.1% | none | none |

Approvals lost = approvals missing versus the baseline conversion applied to the same number of intents; USD is estimated the same way on approved volume and is rough because ticket mix is noisy (the same method gives -3,122 USD, i.e. above baseline, for the period after v3.1). In the window, the -2.52 pp splits into risk blocks -1.99 pp (111 approvals), 3DS abandonment -0.07 pp (4) and approval rate on payments that reached an acquirer -0.46 pp (26).

**Cause.** Risk rules v3 (CHG-0618), the new card-velocity rule. The risk-block rate went from 1.3% at baseline to 3.0% on 18 June and 4.0% on 19 June. Blocked payments never reach an acquirer, so the cascade cannot recover them: this is neither an acquirer-side nor an issuer-side cause.

**Evidence.**
- Timing at both ends: risk-block rate 1.6% (5 of 311) on 18 June before 09:00 and 3.2% (64 of 2,021) after; 2.9% (27 of 926) on 20 June before 15:00 and 1.1% (31 of 2,838) from 15:00 on 20 June to the end of 21 June, when conversion was back at 85.4%.
- Credit and debit were hit alike (19 June risk-block rate: 4.0% credit, 4.1% debit). 3DS abandonment did not drive it (1.4% baseline, 1.7% on 18 June, 1.3% on 19 June).
- Approval side flat (domestic payments sent to acquirers, window): final approval 88.0% to 87.6% (-0.33 pp, 16 approvals; approved USD was above, not below, the baseline expectation). No driver contributed more than 0.5 pp (largest: non-3DS payments -0.50 pp, issuer BR-ISS-01 -0.48 pp, gaming -0.37 pp, acquirer C -0.23 pp), and all domestic payments stayed on routing v12 in baseline and window.
- No first-attempt decline code grew by more than 0.19 pp of payments (largest: acquirer C code 1A, 3DS required, +0.19 pp).
- Retries intact (domestic, 18-19 June): decline map v2.2 throughout; every acquirer and reason code kept the same soft/hard/technical classification and the same cascade rate as baseline.
- Change log for Brazil, 29 May to 21 June 2026: only three changes: Checkout UI v5.2 on 3 June (before the baseline) and the two risk-rule changes above. I found no routing, decline-mapping or partner-notice change in that period.

**Recommended action.**
1. Ask Risk to review what the v3 rule blocked in the window (188 blocks plus 8 review timeouts, 3.5% of intents versus 1.3% at baseline) to separate fraud prevented from false positives. This data has no fraud or chargeback outcomes, so approvals lost is an upper bound if the extra blocks were legitimate customers.
2. Keep tracking the risk-block rate against the 1.3% baseline after v3.1 (1.1% so far, 20 June 15:00 to 21 June).
3. Add risk-block rate to monitoring and stage risk-rule rollouts: the approval anomaly table only covers payments sent to acquirers, so it cannot see this kind of drop.
4. No change needed to routing, acquirers or cascade settings.

**Limits.** The link to the v3 rule rests on timing at both ends, no other change in the period and a flat approval side; the data has no per-rule block reason. Approval-side checks are domestic only; conversion includes cross-border (3.9% of intents at baseline, 4.2% in the window, so no meaningful mix shift). Daily figures come from gold_funnel_daily and window figures from silver_payments, which matches it for 18 June (2,332 intents, 1,947 approved). I did not split the extra blocks by merchant segment or issuer, and I did not drill into the small approval-side movers (gaming, BR-ISS-01).

questions.question: Which acquirer had the higher final approval rate on domestic credit cards in Mexico in July 2026, A or C, and by how much?
questions.answer:

questions.question: Compare the first-attempt approval of Acquirers A and B on domestic debit cards in Mexico in July 2026.
questions.answer:
**Acquirer A had the higher first-attempt approval: 79.8% vs 76.3% for Acquirer B, a gap of 3.45 pp (on the unrounded rates).**

Segment: Mexico, domestic debit cards (is_cross_border = false), 1 to 31 July 2026, local dates. Each payment is attributed to the first acquirer chosen by routing. First-attempt approval = approved on the first attempt / payments sent to an acquirer.

| MX, domestic debit, July 2026 | Acquirer A | Acquirer B |
|---|---|---|

| Approved on first attempt | 12,072 | 11,564 |
| **First-attempt approval rate** | **79.8%** | **76.3%** |
| Soft declines (% of payments sent) | 15.6% | 17.5% |
| Hard declines | 3.7% | 4.7% |
| Technical errors / timeouts | 0.9% | 1.4% |

B is higher in all three failure types. Including cascade retries (final approval) the rates are A 83.7% and B 81.9%, so retries narrow the gap but do not close it.

**Is the gap solid?**
- By day: A was above B on 29 of the 31 days. B was ahead only on 2 July (by 0.73 pp) and 8 July (by 0.27 pp).
- By issuer: both acquirers received almost the same issuer mix (each issuer's share differs by less than 1 pp), and A is ahead at all eight issuers (MX-ISS-01 to MX-ISS-08). At the largest one, MX-ISS-01, it is 81.7% vs 77.5%.
- By routing version: the gap shows before and after routing v13 (from 2 July). Under v12 (1 to 2 July, about 740 payments per acquirer) A was at 81.4% and B at 75.5%. Under v13 (2 to 31 July) A was at 79.7% and B at 76.4%.
- Data quality: all 31 days have data for both acquirers. The payment-level table gives the same counts, with no payments flagged as missing the acquirer response.

**Worth knowing**
- The gap widened at month end. On 29, 30 and 31 July A was at 82.5%, 79.1% and 82.7% and B at 74.7%, 74.6% and 72.3%. 31 July was the widest day of the month (10.39 pp). Each acquirer handles roughly 360 to 680 payments a day, so single days are noisy.
- The Mexico change log from 21 June to 31 July lists two changes: routing v13 on 2 July at 09:00 local (10% of MX debit to Acquirer C as an A/B test; C is outside this comparison) and a 3DS SDK upgrade on web checkout on 28 July at 10:00 local (MX, CO).

**Not checked:** I did not run the decline-shift, cascade-health or approval-driver checks, so I am not naming a cause for why B trails A or for the month-end widening, and I cannot say whether either logged change is related. I can run those checks for B vs A, or for 29 to 31 July, if useful.

questions.question: Was there any early warning before the Colombia debit incident of 13 August 2026?
questions.answer:
Yes, partly. A cascade (retry) alert on Acquirer B ran for 7 days before the incident. The daily anomaly monitor and the change log gave no equivalent warning. All times are Bogota; segment is Colombia, debit, domestic, unless noted.

**The warning**
- 6 Aug 08:00: CHG-0806 put decline-code map v2.3 live for Acquirer B. Its description only says 'adds R65 handling'.
- 6 to 12 Aug: the cascade alert table flagged Acquirer B / code 05 (Do not honor) on all 7 days. The retry rate fell from a healthy baseline of 100.0% to 5.0% on 6 Aug (1 of 20 failures) and 0.0% on each day from 7 to 12 Aug (0 of 24 on 12 Aug). On 13 Aug it saw 109 failures, still none retried. This table has no card-type split, so it covers all card types.
- Footprint check (Colombia domestic, all card types, 6 Aug 08:00 to 13 Aug 14:00 vs the 14 days before): B's code 05 went from soft, 100.0% retried, 37.5% recovery to hard, 0.0% retried, 0.0% recovery. It is the only code present in both periods whose classification changed, and A's code 05 kept being retried (97.9% before, 100.0% after). So the change had an effect its description does not list.

**What gave no warning**
- Daily anomaly monitor: no day flagged from 1 Jul to 12 Aug (deviation from the 28-day baseline between -2.18 and +1.79 pp). First flag: 13 Aug, 79.4% vs 86.7% (-7.33 pp).
- Change log (Colombia, 1 Jun to 14 Aug 00:00): 4 entries only (two releases on 3 Jun and 28 Jul, CHG-0806, CHG-0813) and no partner notice (EXT-*). I did not check the footprint of the 28 Jul 3DS SDK release.
- Approval KPIs: in the daily data from 13 Jul to 12 Aug and the hourly data for 13 Aug before 14:00, all domestic debit went to Acquirer A and was stable (83.0% to 88.6% final approval in the busy hours 07:00 to 13:00 on 13 Aug). B had no debit traffic to degrade, so its 151 code-05 failures from 6 Aug to 13 Aug 14:00 were not debit.

**The incident (window sized: 13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:00)**
- CHG-0813 (13 Aug 14:00) sent 100% of CO domestic debit to B (routing v14, cost optimization). The first hour on B was already at 73.2% final approval (56 payments). Traffic was back on A during the 12:00 hour on 14 Aug (17 payments still on B that hour are outside the window). I did not check the change log after 14 Aug 00:00, so I cannot say what ended it.
- Impact over 987 payments: final approval 75.6% vs 86.5% baseline (14 days before), -10.96 pp; 108 lost approvals (746 vs 854 expected); USD 6,219.53 lost approved volume.
- Link to the warning: B's code-05 declines were 13.7% of its payments (A baseline 4.1%) and none were retried; on A that code was retried 98.4% of the time with 21.7% recovery. B also declined more for 3DS-required (1A): 5.2% vs 1.1%, but those were retried. Drivers for the whole of 13 Aug put -6.86 pp of the -7.14 pp change on Acquirer B / routing v14; the largest issuer effect was -1.65 pp. I did not split the -10.96 pp between B's higher first-attempt declines and the missing 05 retries.

**Recommended actions**
1. Confirm whether hard (non-retryable) for code 05 on B was intended; if not, restore retries, and require a retry-behavior check in mapping change reviews.
2. Before moving a segment onto an acquirer with no recent traffic in it, check its open cascade alerts and start with a small share.
3. Send is_alert rows to the owners of recent mapping and routing changes, and add an hourly segment approval alert: the daily monitor only flagged the incident day.

**Not checked:** who received the alerts, whether the mapping was fixed later (the Colombia alert rows end on 14 Aug), and other countries routed to B (CHG-0806 is scoped to Acquirer B as a whole).

questions.question: Which Colombian issuer had the lowest final approval on domestic debit cards during the incident window, from 13 August 2026 14:00 to 14 August 2026 12:10 local time?
questions.answer:
**CO-ISS-07 had the lowest final approval: 65.3% (47 approved of 72 payments sent).**

Segment and window: Colombian domestic (non cross-border) debit cards, payments that reached an acquirer, 13 Aug 2026 14:00 to 14 Aug 2026 12:10 Bogota local time (UTC-5, end time excluded). Final approval includes approvals recovered by cascade. For CO-ISS-07, first-attempt approval was 61.1% and the cascade recovered 3 of its 8 retried payments.

| Issuer | Payments sent | Final approved | Final approval (window) | 14-day baseline | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CO-ISS-07 | 72 | 47 | 65.3% | 84.9% | -19.6 pp |
| CO-ISS-03 | 145 | 105 | 72.4% | 84.8% | -12.4 pp |
| CO-ISS-05 | 96 | 70 | 72.9% | 84.6% | -11.6 pp |
| CO-ISS-02 | 169 | 126 | 74.6% | 87.9% | -13.3 pp |
| CO-ISS-04 | 110 | 84 | 76.4% | 86.1% | -9.7 pp |
| CO-ISS-06 | 118 | 91 | 77.1% | 87.0% | -9.9 pp |
| CO-ISS-01 | 230 | 184 | 80.0% | 87.8% | -7.8 pp |
| CO-ISS-08 | 64 | 52 | 81.3% | 87.0% | -5.7 pp |

Baseline is each issuer's own 14-day baseline from fn_approval_drivers; Change is the window rate minus the baseline.

**Reading the result**
- The bottom of the ranking is not statistically firm. With only 72 payments, CO-ISS-07's approximate 95% margin of error is ±11.0 pp, and the next three issuers (72.4%, 72.9%, 74.6%) are within that margin of its rate. Among issuers with at least 100 payments in the window, the lowest is CO-ISS-03 at 72.4% (145 payments).
- CO-ISS-07 also had the largest fall against its own baseline (84.9% to 65.3%), and that baseline was in line with the other issuers' (84.6% to 87.9%).
- It is not the largest contributor to the segment's drop. The whole segment ran at 75.6% (759 approved of 1,004 sent), -10.95 pp against its 14-day baseline, and all eight issuers were below their own baselines. CO-ISS-07 accounts for -1.41 pp of that because it handled few payments (72 of 1,004); the largest contribution is CO-ISS-02 at -2.25 pp.
- Whole segment by hour: 83.0% to 88.5% in the six hours from 08:00 to 13:59 on 13 Aug, 73.2% in the 14:00 hour, and 84.6% in the 12:00 hour on 14 Aug (the hour the window ends in).

**How I measured:** the window ends at 12:10, which is not a whole hour, so I used payment-level data instead of the hourly or daily tables. For the whole hours 14:00 to 12:00 it matches the hourly table exactly (987 sent, 746 approved, 75.6%), and the per-issuer payment counts match fn_approval_drivers.

**Not checked:** this answers which issuer was lowest, not why. questions.question: Forecast the final approval rate in Mexico for September 2026.
questions.answer:
I can't forecast September 2026 from this data. It covers 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-29, so it has no September records, and the copilot has no forecasting function. Any September number from me would be a guess, not a query result, so I am not giving one. The closest thing the data can answer is how Mexico actually performed, which you can use as a reference.

**Mexico, domestic cards (is_cross_border = false), all card types. Final approval rate = final_approved / payments_sent (includes cascade recoveries):**

| Month | Payments sent | Final approval rate | Lowest to highest day |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-06 (Jun 1-30) | 73,099 | 86.5% | 84.4% to 88.1% |
| 2026-07 (Jul 1-31) | 79,259 | 86.4% | 85.2% to 88.1% |
| 2026-08 (Aug 1-29, last day of data) | 73,283 | 86.5% | 84.9% to 88.2% |

- By card type (domestic): credit 89.2% and debit 82.9% in 2026-08 (Aug 1-29); credit 89.0% and debit 82.9% in 2026-07.
- Cross-border cards are excluded above (copilot default). They approve much lower: 74.2% in 2026-08 (3,001 payments sent).

**What I checked**
- Anomalies: no MX credit or debit day is flagged as an abnormal drop in gold_anomalies_daily (whole table, data through 2026-08-29). The flag needs a drop of at least 3 pp below baseline, so smaller dips (for example the week of 2026-08-10) would not be flagged.
- Change log, entries from 2026-08-15 onward: CHG-0815 (2026-08-15, decline-mapping hotfix v2.3.1 on acquirer B: R05 reclassified as soft and retryable) and CHG-0820 (2026-08-20, two new MX merchants onboarded). Nothing is logged after 2026-08-20. I did not measure what either change did to the rate, and I did not review changes before 2026-08-15.
- Not run: the driver, decline-code and cascade diagnosis, because this question does not need them. Three months of data is also too short to say anything about September seasonality.

**How to read this:** the monthly rate held at 86.4% to 86.5% from June to August. Using that level for September means assuming routing, acquirer behavior, issuer mix and merchant mix stay as they were; the data cannot confirm that. If useful, I can split the reference by acquirer or card type, or run the diagnosis on the lowest week (starting 2026-08-10) to see what moved.

What I can do instead, read-only:

2. List the incident windows together with the production changes around them (routing changes and rollbacks, decline-mapping changes, partner notices) from the change log, so the dashboard can annotate the incidents instead of hiding them.
3. Size what each incident cost in approvals and USD against its baseline.

Note that the tables I can query have no per-payment incident flag, so incidents are identified by those daily flags and the change log, not row by row. If the rows really must be removed at the source, that has to go through the data owners' change process, outside this copilot.
